newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH TT SAYS BROAD 98 PAY DEAL MAY BE DIFFICULT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH TT SAYS BROAD 98 PAY DEAL MAY BE DIFFICULT.

text.p: The Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) said on Thursday a broad centralised incomes settlement for 1998 would be desirable, but that it could prove difficult to achieve such a deal.

"It would be desirable to reach a general agreement strengthening our competitiveness but it can become very difficult," TT chairman Jukka Harmala, also CEO of forest industry group Enso Oy , told the TT spring meeting according to the text of a prepared speech.

"Already now many trade unions have expressed their needs to freely solve their own problems, and as a result it may become significantly more difficult to reach uniformity and equality," Harmala said.
The influential Paper Workers' Union is one which has indicated that it migh prefer branch-level pay talks next autumn.
From TT's point of view, competitiveness should be the central measure of the incomes settlement to succeed the one expiring at end-January 1998, Harmala said.

"At this stage there is no reason to reject the thought of a centralised agreement. A centralised incomes settlement can, however, come into question only if all employer and wage earner organisations commit themselves to a possible agreement," he said.

Harmala ruled out any general agreement to reduce working hours. Strict union demands for a general reduction of working hours or for employment guarantees "may endanger the entire round of collective bargaining," he said.
